attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The bridge does not reach NP notin P/poly unless one proves a cofinal family of padded lower bounds or finds a non-artificial carrier whose interface compresses every polynomial target exponent below N^{1+epsilon}.
steps: Fix L=SAT, constants k>=2 and epsilon>0, and legal source length N=n^k.
Assume toward contradiction that SAT has O(n^c)-size circuits for some c<k(1+epsilon).
On a padded input y of length N, check that the last N-n bits are zero using O(N) gates and feed the first n bits into the SAT circuit.
The composed circuit has size O(N+n^c)=O(N+N^{c/k}). Since max(1,c/k)<1+epsilon, this is below N^{1+epsilon} for large N.
This contradicts the source lower bound for Pad_k(SAT), yielding SAT notin SIZE(n^c).
Auditing the P/poly target shows that fixed k leaves all exponents c>=k(1+epsilon) untouched.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: No source lower bound is proved. The padding transfer is relativizing and syntactic, and the remaining unrestricted-circuit lower-bound obligation remains subject to natural-proofs and nonuniformity barriers.

assumptions: k and epsilon are fixed constants, and N ranges over legal lengths N=n^k.
The padding predicate is exact-zero padding, so invalid padded strings are rejected by a linear-size circuit.
Circuit-size classes are nonuniform and use the same fan-in-2 Boolean basis on source and target.
The exponent margin is strict: c/k<1+epsilon, absorbing constant factors for sufficiently large n.
definitions: source object: Pad_k(SAT), the exact-zero k-padding of SAT with total length N=n^k, measured against nonuniform fan-in-2 Boolean circuits of size N^{1+epsilon}.
target object: SAT_n measured against nonuniform fan-in-2 Boolean circuits of size n^c; the target consequence is SAT notin SIZE(n^c), not P != NP.
controlled interface: projection to the first n input bits plus an O(N)-size padding-validity checker before running the target circuit.
target-preserving condition: any O(n^c)-size circuit family for SAT must compose into an O(N+N^{c/k})-size circuit family for Pad_k(SAT) with the same basis and no hidden advice.

equations.valid_when: Valid when the source lower-bound model is explicitly restricted to legal padded lengths N=n^k.

equations.label: E2_composition_upper_bound

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any composition overhead above N^{1+epsilon}, any basis mismatch, or any attempted conclusion for c>=k(1+epsilon).
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quantitative bridge lemma: a barely-superlinear padded-source lower bound transfers to a bounded-polynomial SAT circuit lower bound with exponent ceiling k(1+epsilon).
candidate_lemmas.statement: For fixed k>=2 and epsilon>0, a lower bound SIZE(Pad_k(SAT)_N)>N^{1+epsilon} against nonuniform fan-in-2 Boolean circuits implies SAT notin SIZE(n^c) for every c<k(1+epsilon). This is a valid route-level bridge, not a proof of P != NP.

assumptions: k is fixed before the target exponent d is chosen.
The only available transfer inequality is C(Pad_k(SAT)_N)<=O(N+N^{d/k}).
definitions: source object: one fixed padded SAT carrier Pad_k(SAT) at barely-superlinear threshold N^{1+epsilon}.
target object: the full class P/poly, equal to the union over all polynomial-size exponents SIZE(n^d).
controlled interface: the same padding composition map from target circuits to source circuits.
target-preserving condition: the bridge must cover every target exponent d to certify P/poly exclusion.

equations.valid_when: Valid when k and epsilon are fixed constants independent of the target circuit exponent.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The lemma would fail only if an additional magnification theorem compressed all P/poly exponents to N^{1+epsilon} for this same fixed source object.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Negative guardrail: blocks the invalid quantifier jump from one barely-nontrivial lower bound to NP notin P/poly.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A single fixed-k lower bound for Pad_k(SAT) at threshold N^{1+epsilon} cannot by this interface imply SAT notin P/poly; it only rules out target exponents below k(1+epsilon).

assumptions: epsilon is fixed across the family.
For every c, the source lower bound holds for all sufficiently large legal lengths of the chosen k.
definitions: source object: the family {Pad_k(SAT):k>=2} with the same barely-superlinear threshold N^{1+epsilon}.
target object: SAT against all polynomial-size nonuniform Boolean circuit families.
controlled interface: choose k after naming the target exponent c, then apply L1.
target-preserving condition: the lower-bound proof must be uniform in the sense of covering cofinally many k, not merely one convenient padding length.

equations.valid_when: Valid when each chosen k supplies an eventual lower bound on all legal padded lengths.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any proof that supplies only finitely many k values or lets epsilon shrink so fast that c<k(1+epsilon) is not achieved.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Promotion criterion identifying the exact quantifier strength needed for a P/poly consequence.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If for some epsilon>0 and every target exponent c there exists k with c<k(1+epsilon) and Pad_k(SAT) requires size greater than N^{1+epsilon}, then SAT notin P/poly. This promotion is logically valid but turns the source obligation into an infinite cofinal lower-bound family.

Immediate target is SAT notin SIZE(n^c) for c<k(1+epsilon); P/poly requires the cofinal k-family criterion.
The transfer relativizes and does not evade natural proofs; it is outside no known barrier by itself and supplies no nonalgebrizing ingredient.

falsifier: model mismatch occurs if the source lower bound is for AC0, formulas, or uniform circuits while the composed circuit is unrestricted nonuniform P/poly.
falsifier: nonuniform leakage occurs if the padding parser or length selector uses advice not counted in the source circuit size.
falsifier: an infinitely-often source lower bound is not valid for excluding eventual SIZE(n^c) target circuits without matching quantifiers.
falsifier: a natural-proofs-style source argument for unrestricted circuits must explain why it is non-natural or why pseudorandom-function assumptions are avoided.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: The exact quantitative transfer is C(Pad_k(SAT)_N)<=O(N+N^{c/k}); hence the barely-superlinear lower bound magnifies only up to target exponent k(1+epsilon). The valid bridge is useful as an exponent-calibrated route lemma, while the fixed-k P/poly claim is blocked by a concrete threshold falsifier rather than by vague folklore.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is conditional on a PRF-like distribution secure against full-truth-table time and supported at the same n^k threshold. It also applies only after the route is formalized as a large constructive truth-table property.
steps: Set N=2^n and suppose the proposed route supplies R_n with constructivity N^c, largeness delta_n >= N^{-a}, and usefulness against SIZE(n^k).
The target bridge says R_n(SAT_n)=1 for infinitely many n, hence SAT_n has no size n^k circuit on those n if the interface is target-preserving.
Let D_n be a pseudorandom distribution supported on n-bit functions computed by circuits of size n^k.
Because R_n is useful, every sample from D_n is rejected: Pr_{g<-D_n}[R_n(g)=1]=0.
Because R_n is large, a uniformly random truth table is accepted with probability at least delta_n.
A distinguisher queries or constructs the full truth table and runs the R_n decider, using time at most N^c+O(N n^k).
The distinguishing advantage is at least delta_n, contradicting security below delta_n/2.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This certifies a barrier-controlled failure mode for one route class. It neither proves PRFs exist nor proves P != NP; it says which proposed lower-bound interfaces are invalid under the natural-proof hypothesis.

assumptions: Constants a,c,k are fixed before the route starts.
R_n is decidable from the complete truth table in time N^c, where N=2^n.
R_n is useful at the exact threshold: no n-input function computed by a circuit of size n^k lies in R_n.

There is a pseudorandom distribution D_n, e.g. from an exponentially secure PRF, supported on functions computed by circuits of size n^k and secure against time N^c+O(N n^k) distinguishers with advantage below N^{-a}/2.
definitions: source object: a family R_n subset {0,1}^{2^n} deciding properties of n-bit Boolean truth tables in time (2^n)^c and having density at least (2^n)^{-a}.
target object: the nonuniform slice lower bound SAT_n notin SIZE(n^k) infinitely often, or the same statement for an NP-complete slice under advice-free length-respecting encodings.
controlled interface: transfer is only R_n(SAT_n)=1 together with R_n cap TT(SIZE(n^k)) empty, with no semantic information about SAT used outside the property test.
target-preserving condition: the encoding of the target slice must map n-bit inputs to one N=2^n bit truth table and must not add advice, promises, or more than polynomial threshold loss.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The route fails this audit if its proposed proof object is large, constructive, and useful in the above sense. A valid falsifier must remove at least one of those three hypotheses while preserving the SAT_n threshold transfer.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is a route-level quarantine lemma, not evidence for P != NP. It converts an intended lower-bound bridge into a concrete barrier violation at density N^{-a} and threshold n^k.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A route that proves SAT_n notin SIZE(n^k) only by exhibiting a poly(N)-constructive, N^{-a}-large truth-table property useful against SIZE(n^k) is conditionally blocked by the Razborov-Rudich natural-proof mechanism. Under exponentially secure pseudorandom functions supported inside SIZE(n^k), the same property is a distinguisher with advantage at least N^{-a}.

assumptions: The proof skeleton contains no arithmetization, interactive-checking, counting, or other explicitly nonrelativizing step.
Cook-style encodings and reductions are asserted to remain valid relative to arbitrary O.
Baker-Gill-Solovay oracle separations are available as external barrier witnesses.
definitions: source object: an oracle-invariant proof skeleton Phi whose definitions, simulations, and diagonal steps commute with adding arbitrary oracle O.
target object: an unrelativized separation P != NP or a nonuniform NP lower bound claimed to imply it.
controlled interface: every use of computation is through oracle-preserving machine simulation, padding, or diagonalization.
target-preserving condition: if Phi proves the target, then for every O the relativized Phi^O proves the corresponding target relative to O.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Any lower-bound route whose target transfer and all intermediate simulations relativize uniformly to every oracle cannot by itself resolve P versus NP, because oracle worlds realize both outcomes.

assumptions: The route has already been classified by L1 as natural unless a named Razborov-Rudich condition is broken.
PRF security is treated as a conditional barrier, not an unconditional theorem.
Any threshold weakening must be explicitly recorded as n^k -> s(n).
definitions: source object: a candidate replacement certificate C_n for hardness of SAT_n.
target object: SAT_n notin SIZE(n^k) or a precisely quantified weaker nonuniform lower bound.
controlled interface: C_n must imply rejection of all circuits at the named threshold and acceptance of the target slice.
target-preserving condition: the escape feature must not be supplied by nonuniform advice encoding the target truth table.

The repair is useful only if it still proves the target-preserving bridge.

Therefore a lower-bound route must name a real escape feature: non-large, nonconstructive, non-truth-table, nonrelativizing, or quantitatively below the PRF threshold. attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing object is a uniform hard-table carrier G. MCSP as a decision language does not supply G within the E time budget, and a nonuniform seed would leak the lower bound into advice.
steps: Define N=2^n and let the MCSP carrier be a uniform algorithm G producing one N-bit table y_n per input length.
Assume the semantic carrier property CktSize(y_n)>N^epsilon for all sufficiently large n.
Construct L_G by taking y_n as the length-n truth table; compute L_G(x) by running G(1^n) and reading the indexed bit.
The running time is N^{O(1)}=2^{O(n)}, hence L_G is in E.
The length-n circuit complexity of L_G equals the circuit complexity of y_n, so the threshold N^epsilon is preserved exactly.
Invoke IW to obtain BPP=P from eventual 2^{epsilon n} hardness in E.
Audit the source: an MCSP decider, a random high-complexity table, or an advice-selected table does not satisfy the source object definition.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The bridge is valid conditional route progress, but constructing G with CktSize(y_n)>2^{epsilon n} is essentially the explicit lower-bound task. It gives BPP=P if supplied, and it does not separate P from NP.

assumptions: Boolean circuits use a fixed finite basis and nonuniform size is measured on n input variables.
The generator G is total and uniform; its description is not length-dependent advice.
The MCSP lower-bound assertion is eventual, not merely infinitely often, when invoking IW.
IW is used only as a derandomization transfer; no P vs NP separation is claimed.
definitions: source object: an MCSP-type hard-table carrier G with semantic promise CktSize(y_n)>2^{epsilon n} for N=2^n and uniform output time N^{O(1)}.
target object: an E-language L_G whose length-n truth table is y_n, plus the standard IW derandomization target BPP=P from eventual exponential worst-case hardness.
controlled interface: map the carrier truth table to the length-n slice of L_G without advice, nonuniform seed choice, promise-dependent decoding, or a reduction that changes N=2^n.

target-preserving condition: the same threshold 2^{epsilon n}=N^{epsilon} holds for the extracted slice for all sufficiently large n, and G remains deterministic uniform with bit recovery in 2^{O(n)} time.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any use of a nonuniform seed, advice string, promise oracle, or infinitely-often-only hard table while still claiming the IW target.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Positive bridge lemma: it formalizes the exact carrier-to-lower-bound-to-derandomization transfer and isolates the missing explicit hard-table construction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Fix epsilon>0. If a deterministic uniform generator G outputs, on input 1^n, a truth table y_n in {0,1}^{2^n} within time 2^{O(n)} and y_n has Boolean circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon n} for all sufficiently large n, then the induced language L_G is in E and has circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon n} on length n. By the Impagliazzo-Wigderson theorem this route-level consequence yields BPP=P, not P != NP.

assumptions: A runs in poly(N) time on an N-bit table.
High-complexity tables exist by counting for s below about 2^n/n.
No additional pseudorandom sampler or hitting-set structure is assumed.
definitions: source object: a decider A for MCSP_s on N-bit truth tables.
target object: an E-explicit hard function family.
controlled interface: only uniform calls to A are allowed; the selected hard table cannot be supplied as advice.
target-preserving condition: the search for y_n must finish in 2^{O(n)} time and preserve threshold s(n).

candidate_lemmas.statement: A polynomial-time decision procedure for MCSP_s does not by itself give an E-explicit function with circuit complexity greater than s(n), because locating a high-complexity truth table by lexicographic search ranges over 2^{2^n} tables.

assumptions: Threshold s is polynomially bounded in N so a small circuit is an NP witness.
C is a named nonuniform model such as AC0, TC0, NC1, or P/poly-size q.
The lower bound is for MCSP as a language on truth-table inputs, not for represented functions.

controlled interface: identity inclusion MCSP_s in NP; no hardness amplification or reduction is used.

candidate_lemmas.statement: If for some circuit class C and polynomial q, the language MCSP_s on N-bit inputs has no C-circuit family of size q(N), then NP is not contained in C-size q on input length N, since MCSP_s is in NP. This is a baseline lower-bound consequence, not an extraction theorem.

dependency_updates.description: Carrier must be a uniform hard-table generator, not merely MCSP, an MCSP oracle, or a distribution containing hard tables.
Truth-table extraction preserves E-uniformity and circuit threshold exactly when the generator runs in N^{O(1)} time and uses no advice.
Explicitness means deterministic production or bit recovery within 2^{O(n)} time for every sufficiently large n; promise search over all truth tables violates it.

The bridge is relativizing and not natural-proof-sensitive by itself; the hard-table construction would need non-natural or otherwise barrier-escaping content if it implied strong circuit lower bounds.
